title: Guardian Runner for Phased Autodeploy of Optimize Suggestions
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description: Problem: The Optimize service produces batching and KV-cache recommendations that materially reduce per-token cost. Operators need a safe, auditable, and reversible path to auto-apply these recommendations for eligible customers without risking latency regressions or quality drop-offs. Existing staged rollouts focus on simple percent-based canaries but lack a unified gated runner that ties recommendation metadata, simulated traffic verification, and ops approvals together.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Guardian Runner accepts an Optimize suggestion payload and expands it into a phased deployment plan (shadow -> partial traffic -> majority -> full) with per-step guard rails. 2) Each phase runs a simulated-traffic verifier and a telemetry check that evaluates latency (P50/P95), errors, throughput, cost delta, and eval-based quality score against the baseline. 3) If thresholds are exceeded, the runner halts and creates a rollback or escalation ticket; operator can also acknowledge to continue. 4) All actions are auditable (who, when, why) and reversible via single API call. 5) Integration tests cover happy path, simulated failure, and manual-approval path.
runbook: Runbook: Guardian Runner emergency stop: POST /api/v1/guardian/{id}/halt
Rollback: POST /api/v1/guardian/{id}/rollback -> triggers config revert and traffic re-routing
architecture_notes: The Guardian Runner is a control-plane orchestrator. It composes three subsystems: 1) recommendation reconciler (ingests Optimize suggestions and normalizes into plan steps), 2) verifier (simulated traffic harness + metric evaluator), 3) enactor (applies config diffs to serving pools with traffic partitioning). Communication is via existing event bus and uses feature flags to gate experimental behavior.
safety_criteria: Metric thresholds and decision rules encoded as policy definitions. Example rules: P95 latency increase > 15% OR error rate increase > 0.5% -> halt; quality eval score drop > 3% absolute -> halt and alert PM/Reliability. Cost delta > -30% is OK; cost increase is forbidden unless explicitly operator-acknowledged.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluator and plan expander. Integration test that runs in staging with traffic replay tool (replay ID TBD). Chaos test that simulates a model variant returning slower KV-cache response. End-to-end smoke in dedicated test pools. Add synthetic prompts for critical eval-set monitored by quality pipeline.

open_risks: Unmodeled distribution shifts: synthetic replay may not uncover real-world prompt surface causing silent quality regressions.
Operator fatigue: noisy halts could lead to routine overrides; need a feedback loop to adjust policies.
Cross-customer isolation: ensuring that a partial traffic partition never leaks state across tenants when KV-cache keys are shared requires strict namespace enforcement.
Rollback latency: reverting a config across large dedicated fleets may take several minutes, impacting short-lived traffic spikes.
mitigations: Include canary cohorts with actual customer traffic for early adopters and require consent from customer before autoapply.
Add adaptive escalation: if same halt occurs 3 times within 24h, block autoapply for that recommendation class and surface to PM.
Enforce tenant namespace at enactor layer and validate with unit tests and an integration test that asserts keyspace separation.
Precompute revert diffs and warm rollback pipelines to reduce time-to-revert; measure and SLO the rollback time.
